output.answer_markdown: NRG says that acquiring or disposing of businesses, assets or retail customer books involves a number of risks [1]. For acquisitions, these include failing to identify material problems during due diligence, overpaying for assets or customers, being unable to retain customers, and being unable to arrange financing [2]. Integration also requires substantial resources and may not succeed [3]. For dispositions, the risks relate to employment matters, counterparties, regulators and other stakeholders, separating the disposed assets, managing the ongoing business, and unknown risks, and NRG may face material trailing liabilities [4]. Any of these risks may lead to costly disputes or litigation [5]. There is no assurance that acquisitions will perform as expected or that their returns will support the debt and capital expenditures taken on for them, or that NRG will realize the anticipated benefits of dispositions [6]. If the expected returns or benefits are not realized, NRG's results of operations, cash flows and financial condition could be adversely affected [7].
